title: POC scoping: Archipelago inference cost & benchmark kickoff
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC focused on unit economics for real-time inference on market-alerts product. Agreed success criteria: <50ms  p95 for single-turn queries on hosted or dedicated variant (final SLO TBD), evidence of sub-$0.0008 per-token effective cost with batching/caching knobs, and privacy compliance checklist (SOC2 + KMS). Next: baseline benchmark run, sample payload, security packet, pricing sheet.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-14 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~62 min | Attendees: Maya, Jordan (Redwood); Priya, Diego, Aisha, Evan, Marcela (Archipelago)
[00:00] Maya: hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll run through scope for the POC today, quick intro - i'm Maya, im the AE, Jordan is our solutions engineer, Luis is on deck for ops follow-up.
[00:18] Priya: thanks, quick context — archipelago is building an event-driven market alerts feed, latency is customer-facing, cost matters because we serve millions of requests daily, so unit econ is central.
[00:31] Jordan: great. so the goal of this POC is to give you realistic per-token estimates and a benchmark plan, we want to model batching, KV caching, and compare hosted vs dedicated. is that accurate?
[00:43] Diego: yes. also want to test 4k context tails and streaming responses, our prompts include long context with user state.
[00:55] Aisha: on infra side — we may need VPC peering for private deployment but we want to evaluate hosted first. can you confirm what data leaves our vpc in hosted mode?
[01:10] Maya: short answer: metadata goes to control plane, payload options are configurable; we will send security packet. Marcela will want SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration details.
[01:20] Marcela: yep, and also audit logs, retention policies — can we get sample log format?
[01:28] Luis: i'll attach sample audit log export after the call.
[01:33] Jordan: ok, moving to workload sizing — Diego, can you describe qps patterns, payload size and expected tokens per request?
[01:42] Diego: typical p95 QPS is 120, burst to 700 for major events; average prompt tokens ~450, completion target avg 60 tokens but can spike to 400 for long-form.
[01:56] Evan: we consider a single prompt/response to be one transaction; streaming matters for UX so latency target is tight.
[02:05] Jordan: for cost modeling we'll treat two main workloads: short replies (avg 60 completion tokens) and long replies (avg 400). We'll model per-token cost, and then effective per-interaction cost after batching and KV cache reuse.
[02:20] Priya: what's realistic per-token baseline on Redwood hosted?
[02:26] Maya: rough ballpark depends on model. For a 4-bit quantized LLM in Redwood hosted, raw token processing cost equivalent might be around $0.0009-0.0015/token w/o batching; batching + caching can reduce it by 40-70% depending on reuse. that's approximate.
[02:45] Diego: that spread is big — we'll need concretely measured numbers.
[02:49] Jordan: agreed. POC steps: 1) baseline run using a smallest reasonable model variant on hosted to capture latency & raw tokens/s; 2) run with batching knobs (batch size sweep) and with KV/prefix caching enabled; 3) a dedicated run if needed for tail latency. We'll provide a benchmark harness to run these.
[03:05] Aisha: timeline? we have an exec review on 6/30, need results before that.
[03:12] Maya: so six weeks is tight but doable if we prioritize. Week 1: setup, security review + data handoff. Week 2: baseline runs. Week 3: batching/caching optimization. Week 4: dedicated/throughput tests if required. Week 5: cost model consolidation. Week 6: final report + exec deck.
[03:30] Priya: success criteria from our side: a) validated per-interaction cost under $0.0012 for core use-case; b) p95 latency under 200ms for short replies (we can relax for long replies); c) reproducible benchmark and runbook. If you can meet those we'll look to scope dedicated capacity.
[03:47] Jordan: noted — we'll reason about p95 differently for streaming. that 200ms p95 is aggressive for single token generation; we should scoreboard by route.
[03:55] Diego: also need to see tokenization differences — tokens per prompt vary by tokenizer.
[04:02] Jordan: yes we'll publish tokenization counts and align on the exact model checkpoint.
[04:08] [short crosstalk] Evan: how do you account for KV cache warmup?
[04:12] Jordan: we'll run a warmup phase and measure hit rates. caching scenarios: session-level KV vs prefix-level; effectiveness depends on prompt reuse. we'll show hit rate vs cost curves.
[04:26] Maya: on pricing — we can give a provisional pricing sheet for hosted POC; dedicated capacity pricing is commit-based and will change effective per-token.
[04:37] Priya: our budget for POC is $18k–$25k to run this test and build a decision paper.
[04:45] Maya: ok that helps, we'll aim to keep infra spend within that and propose where host vs dedicated makes sense.
[04:52] Marcela: technical security questions: can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[04:57] Jordan: yes, KMS integrations supported for Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with KMS options. We'll provide the KMS integration spec.
[05:06] Marcela: and are logs stored in your control plane? retention?
[05:09] Luis: retention configurable; we'll send default retention and deletion flow.
[05:15] [Timestamps jump ahead as Jordan goes into benchmark details]
[05:35] Jordan: benchmark plan detail — we'll run three phases: latency profile (p50/p90/p95), throughput scaling (sustained qps with ping-pong), and cost sweep (vary batch sizes and cache hit rates). For batch sweep we recommend testing batch sizes of 4, 8, 16, 32 with varying max latency SLOs.
[05:58] Diego: do you support dynamic batching or is it fixed?
[06:02] Jordan: runtime supports continuous batching with latency-aware bins; you can configure target latency and maximum batch size. It can also fall back to an unbatched fast path.
[06:12] Priya: for our interactive flows we need sub-200ms p95 for short queries at ~150 qps — is that plausible on hosted?
[06:20] Jordan: plausible with small model or higher CUDAs; if not, Dedicated with pinned GPUs is the fallback. We'll test both.
[06:28] Evan: also want to quantify tail cost — when batch sizes drop, effective per-token goes up, we need to model percent of requests that are batched.
[06:36] Jordan: yes we'll instrument request distribution and produce a cost heatmap: cost vs batch hit rate vs latency.
[06:42] [10-minute mark] Priya: what about model variants and quantization?
[06:47] Jordan: we'll test a float16 baseline, and a quantized 4-bit variant (Q4) to show tradeoffs. Quantization reduces compute cost but may slightly change quality; we'll run A/B on a small eval set you provide.
[06:59] Diego: what's expected delta on quality?
[07:02] Jordan: depends but often within 1–3% on our eval metrics; we will flag any regressions.
[07:10] Maya: ok let's talk data handoff — Diego, you'll provide a representative sample of 2k requests and a small eval set of 200 prompts for quality checks. Also sample traffic distribution (qps histogram).
[07:23] Diego: yes, we can share that by EOD Monday.
[07:27] Maya: great. next, benchmarks — what artifacts will Redwood deliver?
[07:32] Jordan: benchmark harness (scripted load runner), results spreadsheet with pivot tables, latency percentiles, batch histograms, token metrics, and a cost model workbook that accounts for hosted per-token rates, batching multipliers, cache hit rate, and discounting for reserved dedicated capacity.
[07:52] Priya: will you include estimated infra hours for integration?
[07:55] Luis: yes we'll include an ops estimate and recommended minimal config for a pilot (region, gpu type, mem).
[08:01] Evan: do you have prior examples or case study numbers?
[08:04] Maya: we can share anonymized case studies of fintech customers showing 40–60% cost reduction after batching/caching; i'll link one in the follow-up.
[08:12] Marcela: for compliance, can you provide an SOC2 package and a list of subprocessor locations?
[08:17] Luis: yes, we'll attach SOC2 and the subprocessor list to the security packet.
[08:21] [Roundtable on success metrics and acceptance criteria]
[08:30] Priya: final acceptance should include a reproducible runbook, cost < $0.0012 per interaction for core flows, p95 <200ms for short path, identified model and deployment recommendation.
[08:42] Maya: agreed, we'll aim to deliver a deck that maps to those criteria.
[08:47] Diego: who will run the dedicated run if needed? we'll need an SE or ops contact.
[08:52] Jordan: i'll own the dedicated runs, coordinate with Aisha for peering and firewall rules.
[08:57] Aisha: action for infra — open a ticket with IP ranges and accept rules, i'll get it to our team.
[09:05] [Noise / overlap]
[09:12] Maya: quick questions from contract side — budget constraints? you said 18–25k. is that for the hosted-only approach?
[09:21] Priya: yes that's the POC budget we have. if dedicated is required we'll need an estimate and business case.
[09:27] Maya: ok we'll design the plan to stay in budget for hosted baseline and reserve the dedicated runs as an add-on.
[09:34] Jordan: last technical note — we will capture tokenization deltas by running tokenizer locally against your corpus; that will be part of the baseline.
[09:43] Evan: and if we need advanced routing (region fallback) can Redwood support multi-region routing?
[09:49] Jordan: yes, smart routing supported; for POC we can test single region and a quick failover test.
[09:56] [Wrap-up and next steps recap]
[10:00] Maya: recap — deliverables: security packet (SOC2,KMS spec, logs format), benchmark harness and instructions, initial baseline runs, cost model workbook, pricing sheet, and a final results deck. Timeline: Diego sends sample data by Monday; week-by-week plan as discussed; exec-ready deck by 6/25 to 6/30 window.
[10:23] Diego: confirmed sample data Monday.
[10:27] Priya: will you include a short note on limitations and assumptions in the model? we need that for the exec.
[10:33] Jordan: yes assumptions & methodology included.
[10:36] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark runs and attach the security docs.
[10:45] (meeting adjourned)

Notes: transcript includes typical ASR errors and occasional label mismatches; timestamps are approximate and meant to reflect pacing rather than verbatim timing.
